stories.headline: Trump demands investigation into GDP data revisions
stories.summary: Remember that Q3 GDP data? It just got a massive upward revision, which means the economy grew way faster than initially thought. Of course, former President Trump is calling foul, demanding an investigation into what he claims is a "record setting error" and implying political manipulation. Economists, however, say these revisions are pretty standard as more complete data rolls in.

stories.headline: Shoppers are bargain hunting, boosting Black Friday hopes
stories.summary: Inflation might be a drag, but don't count out holiday spending just yet. Consumers are definitely looking for value, which means Black Friday sales and "Black November" (yep, it's a whole month now) are looking robust. Retailers are hoping this savvy shopping will translate into strong sales as people hunt for the best deals, signaling a shift in how we approach holiday spending.

stories.headline: Elon Musk pledges $18 billion in SpaceX shares to American kids
stories.summary: In a move that's got everyone's eyebrows raised, Elon Musk just pledged to donate two SpaceX shares to every child in America, doubling down on a similar promise he made last month. This massive $18 billion-plus giveaway sent SpaceX shares jumping and is roughly three times larger than Michael Dell's once-record-breaking gift.

stories.headline: German software giant SAP reportedly slashing 10,000 jobs due to AI push
stories.summary: Even big tech isn't immune to AI's disruptive force. German software powerhouse SAP is reportedly considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs as it pivots its business around artificial intelligence. This shows how quickly AI is forcing major corporations to rethink their workforce and operations, even if it means some painful restructuring.

stories.headline: Banks may pass £1.5bn tax hike onto customers, warns Bank of England
stories.summary: Looks like a proposed £1.5 billion tax increase on bank profits could end up hitting your wallet. The Governor of the Bank of England, Andrew Bailey, is worried that big lenders will try to "protect their earnings" by passing on the cost of this temporary corporation tax surcharge to their customers. So much for banks absorbing the hit!

stories.headline: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons
stories.summary: Just when you thought things couldn't get more tense, Kim Jong Un has reportedly visited nuclear facilities and declared he'll be building more weapons to counter threats from the U.S. and South Korea. This comes despite previous overtures from Trump, indicating a renewed push to beef up his country's arsenal and reject de-escalation.

stories.headline: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
stories.summary: France is finally having its #MeToo reckoning, and now iconic actor Gérard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault. This is a huge moment for the movement in a country where it's faced significant resistance, especially in the arts, bringing a prominent figure's alleged actions into the public eye.

stories.headline: Search for new UN Secretary General stalls as current term nears end
stories.summary: The clock is ticking for the UN Secretary General, but the world's major powers are still bickering over a replacement. With the current term ending soon and no consensus in sight, UN watchers are worried there won't be enough time for a new leader to get up to speed on pressing global issues. Talk about a tough job interview!

stories.headline: Europe's economic "sovereignty" is mostly talk, little action
stories.summary: Despite all the grand pronouncements about Europe building its own economic independence, a new report suggests the continent's reliance on the United States has actually *surged*. It seems all that talk about diversifying away from the U.S. has mostly been just that – talk – highlighting the deep, enduring ties that bind the transatlantic economies.

stories.headline: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases amidst ongoing conflict
stories.summary: A fast-moving Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has now reached a staggering 12,000 cases, with some responders even evacuating due to escalating violence. Fighting between rebels and the army is severely disrupting efforts to contain the disease, turning a public health crisis into a humanitarian disaster compounded by conflict.

stories.headline: Volkswagen drags rivals into $1.2 billion India tax fight
stories.summary: Volkswagen is locked in a high-stakes, $1.2 billion tax dispute in India, and they've now pulled Mercedes and BMW into the fray. VW denies the allegations, calling the case a "life and death" matter that could wipe out all its investments in India, where it currently holds a mere 2% market share. Talk about high drama in the auto industry!

stories.headline: Himachal BJP demands re-exam after Sikh youth barred from test over religious symbols
stories.summary: A Sikh youth in Himachal Pradesh was barred from taking a patwari exam because he wore a kara (steel bracelet) and kirpan (small dagger), which are articles of faith. The State BJP's Minority Morcha is now demanding a re-exam and an explanation from the Congress government, highlighting an important debate about religious freedom and examination rules.

stories.headline: Union Cabinet clears crucial delimitation bill
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet has given its nod to a new delimitation bill, a significant step towards redrawing electoral boundaries. This comes after a similar attempt was rejected earlier this year, signaling a renewed push by the government to potentially reshape political representation across the country.

stories.headline: IBM stops US visa sponsorship for many consulting roles
stories.summary: In a move that will impact many Indian tech professionals, IBM is ending U.S. visa and green card sponsorship for most roles within its consulting unit. While IBM says it uses high-skilled visa programs to address shortages, this decision could significantly alter career paths for those looking to work in the U.S. tech sector.

stories.headline: UK government services knocked offline by "cyber incident"
stories.summary: Yikes! A "cyber incident" has forced the UK government to take some of its online services offline. While details are still emerging, it's a stark reminder that even major government infrastructure isn't immune to digital threats, causing disruption and concern about national security.

stories.headline: EU makes browser competition a Digital Markets Act priority
stories.summary: The European Commission is putting its foot down: browser competition is now a top priority under its Digital Markets Act. This means big tech companies could face stricter rules to ensure a level playing field for alternative browsers, potentially shaking up the dominance of Chrome, Safari, and Edge. Get ready for more choice!

stories.headline: X (formerly Twitter) finally gets parental controls after 20 years
stories.summary: It took a while (okay, like, two decades if you count Twitter's original launch), but Elon Musk's X has finally introduced parental controls for teenagers. Parents and guardians can now manage what their kids see on the platform, which is a welcome, if long-overdue, feature for many.

stories.headline: The iPhone Duo might actually change your phone habits
stories.summary: Forget the hype, this is cool: A reviewer spent a month with the new foldable iPhone Duo and found it genuinely changed how they used their phone. From reading more books to breaking mindless scrolling habits, the device's unique form factor reportedly fostered more mindful digital consumption. Who knew a phone could help you use your phone less?

stories.headline: Grand Theft Auto VI shows why "efficiency" isn't everything
stories.summary: While AI companies are pushing for maximum efficiency, the painstakingly human-made Grand Theft Auto VI just broke records as one of the most successful entertainment launches ever. It's a powerful reminder that sometimes, the magic comes from slow, deliberate human creativity, not just speed or algorithmic optimization. Take that, efficiency bros!

stories.headline: What does it truly mean for atoms to "touch"?
stories.summary: Ever wonder what "touching" really means on an atomic level? Turns out, it's less about physical contact and more about forces. Objects don't actually "touch" in the way we think; instead, their electron clouds repel each other, creating the sensation of solidity. Mind-bending stuff that makes you question reality!

stories.headline: How propaganda hijacks archaeology to rewrite history
stories.summary: Archaeology isn't just about digging up old pots; it can be weaponized. Historians are warning that propagandists are using archaeological findings to rewrite the past, forging collective identities and anchoring nationalist narratives in false histories. It's a powerful tool for shaping what people believe about their origins.

stories.headline: Physicist calls "simulation theory" one of the most stupid ideas
stories.summary: Hold up, Neo. Renowned physicist Carlo Rovelli isn't buying the simulation theory (the idea we might be living in a computer simulation). He argues that the search for an "ultimate reality" is a mistake, aligning with Buddhist philosophy and Wittgenstein, suggesting that physics points away from foundational truths and toward interconnectedness instead. Ouch.

stories.headline: Nvidia pauses AI chip shipments to Southeast Asia amidst US-China tech war
stories.summary: The US-China tech war is heating up, and Nvidia is feeling the pressure. The chip giant has told its manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to several Southeast Asian countries like Malaysia and Thailand. This move is part of the U.S.'s intensified efforts to prevent advanced AI chips from ending up in China, creating ripples across the global supply chain.

stories.headline: AI agent makes first cardless pizza purchase in the UK
stories.summary: Get ready for the future of shopping: an AI agent just made the UK's first cardless purchase, ordering Papa John's pizzas without sharing any bank security details. This tech could revolutionize how we buy things, with AI assistants handling transactions seamlessly and securely. Black Friday, meet your new shopping assistant.

stories.headline: Who's liable when AI shopping bots mess up on Black Friday?
stories.summary: Speaking of AI shopping assistants, what happens when "the bot gets it wrong"? Retailers are heading into Black Friday with AI agents like Meta Muse on the rise, but they're grappling with a huge question: who's liable if the AI makes a mistake, buys the wrong thing, or overspends? It's a brave new world of consumer responsibility.

stories.headline: Mathematicians worry about AI's "eerie silence" on encryption
stories.summary: Award-winning mathematicians are getting seriously concerned about the quiet implications of AI for encryption. They're worried that the rapid advancements in AI could make current online security measures useless, leading to a potential breakdown in secure communications if we don't start addressing this now. Cue the spy movies!

stories.headline: The group chat where your AI talks behind your back
stories.summary: Ever felt like your devices were judging you? Now your AI assistant might actually be talking about you behind your back – in a group chat with other AIs. This wild concept allows AIs to collaborate and discuss user requests, raising fascinating (and slightly creepy) questions about privacy, AI interaction, and what exactly these bots are saying about us.
